rule.description: A shared trait declares capability-probing members (Option-flavored report-or-disclaim queries, not narrowed trait-object views) for which a strict majority of implementors provide inert Ok(None)/None bodies or inherit an equally inert default, while at least one implementor provides a real implementation. One row is reported per offending trait member and one row per inert implementor stub; the trait must be declared and implemented in-crate with at least two impl blocks.

checks.description: Trait members whose capability is genuinely implemented by a minority of implementors and therefore force inert stubs onto the majority.
checks.detected_relation: trait member -> majority-inert capability probe on one shared interface
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The interface exceeds the dependency boundary of most implementors: every one of them must carry and dispatch through members it cannot meaningfully implement, which is the interface-segregation violation.

matches.evidence: Trait member get_exif_rotation_flag is a capability query answered with a real implementation by 2 of 7 implementors (MozJpegDecoder, ZenDecoder); the other 5 carry inert "Ok(None)" bodies (GifDecoder, ImagePngDecoder, JpegDecoder, LibPngDecoder, WebPDecoder), so every implementor and consumer of the shared trait must depend on this member although most cannot supply it.

Trait member last_frame_delay is a capability query answered with a real implementation by 2 of 7 implementors (GifDecoder, ZenDecoder); the other 5 carry inert "Ok(None)" bodies (ImagePngDecoder, JpegDecoder, LibPngDecoder, MozJpegDecoder, WebPDecoder), so every implementor and consumer of the shared trait must depend on this member although most cannot supply it.

Trait member get_loop_count is a capability query answered with a real implementation by 1 of 7 implementors (GifDecoder); the other 6 carry inert "Ok(None)" bodies (ImagePngDecoder, JpegDecoder, LibPngDecoder, MozJpegDecoder, WebPDecoder, ZenDecoder), so every implementor and consumer of the shared trait must depend on this member although most cannot supply it.

Trait member estimate_decode_resources is a capability query answered with a real implementation by 1 of 7 implementors (ZenDecoder); the other 6 carry inert "Ok(None)" bodies (GifDecoder, ImagePngDecoder, JpegDecoder, LibPngDecoder, MozJpegDecoder, WebPDecoder), so every implementor and consumer of the shared trait must depend on this member although most cannot supply it.

checks.description: Implementors of the shared trait that satisfy required capability members with inert bodies.
checks.detected_relation: implementor -> inert stub of a required capability member
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Each stub is a concrete implementor forced to depend on (implement, and let consumers dispatch through) an interface member outside its capability boundary, instead of a focused interface containing only what it uses.

excluded.reason: An execution-hook vtable entry with an inert default, not a capability probe: it has no result-option report-or-disclaim shape on a capability boundary and is served by no capability consumer, so it does not model the fat-interface relation this rule targets.
The write path interface has a single required member shared by all encoders, so no member is majority-inert on that trait.
Inherent methods on the concrete bridge type are not trait members; they are the capability providers the trait impl forwards to, not interface surface forced onto implementors.
